text:
sam.release: deploybot blocked the staging->prod promotion for release/2026.03.21 :warning:

sam.release: reason: eu ECR manifestlist published but arm64 submanifest missing provenance annotation (cosign) — deploybot refused promotion.

deploy-bot: [automated] promotion-check FAILED for image: eu.gcr.redwood/release/2026.03.21:manifestlist
```
> error: provenance-check: submanifest arch=arm64 missing signature/annotation 'cosign-attestation'
> action: hold promotion, notify #eng-infra
```

maria.prod: ack. we had a flaky arm64 job in staging CI earlier today, wonder if that explains it.

jun.infra: looking now — logs show arm64 push completed but cosign upload step errored with HTTP 503 to timestamp-verifier.

jun.infra: command output:
```
cosign upload --key kms://projects/... --payload manifest-arm64.json
Error: 503 service unavailable: timestamp-verifier
```

tony.oncall: can we do a targeted re-sign for the arm64 submanifest instead of rebuilding the whole multiarch image? want minimal blast radius during the change window. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jun.infra: we can re-run cosign sign on the manifest digest for arm64 and attach attestation, but docker registry requires a manifestlist-level index update to reference the signed blob. deploybot supports a targeted republish flow (`--republish-submanifest`) but it only runs in staging by default.

maria.prod: what are the tradeoffs? re-signing only is faster but might leave an inconsistent manifestlist until we update index. full rebuild will produce clean artifacts but costs time. our change window for prod promotion is 30m left.

sam.release: current canary is at 5% prod traffic, no errors reported. We should avoid rolling back if possible. proposal: manual targeted re-sign + deploybot republish-submanifest to staging, run quick canary sanity, then promote. If anything flaky, roll back to previous pinned digest.

tony.oncall: agree with minimal approach. I'll stand by to trigger rollback if SLOs break. rollback criteria: 3xx/4xx/5xx spike >5% or latency 2x baseline for 5min.

jun.infra: I'll attempt targeted re-sign now, will use the staging cosign key and then request manual override to allow republish to prod once canary sanity passes.

ci-bot: queued job #4587: republish-submanifest (arch=arm64) triggered by jun.infra.

deploy-bot: [manual] republish-submanifest started: job=4587, target=eu.gcr.redwood/release/2026.03.21, arch=arm64

jun.infra: quick note — need Maria to sign off on a short release note update that documents this targeted republish and that no user-facing changes expected. release notes must mention the pinned fallback digest in case we roll back.

maria.prod: will update release notes and add a short line: "Hotfix: republished arm64 attestation for release/2026.03.21 — no functional changes." Will also add rollback digest: `sha256:af12...cdef`.

deploy-bot: republish-submanifest completed SUCCESS. cosign attestation present for arm64 submanifest.

deploy-bot: re-running promotion-check... OK. promotion allowed to proceed under canary -> gradual rollout policy.

sam.release: proceeding to promote to canary 10% now. tagging: prod tag unchanged (we keep same semver), backend pinned digest recorded in release notes.

tony.oncall: monitoring. setting temporary alert to catch any arm64-only regresses. :eyes:

maria.prod: release notes pushed to docs repo and changelog updated. linking PR: https://git.redwood/docs/pulls/1024

sam.release: thanks team. keeping thread open until canary reaches 30% or we hit rollback criteria.

jun.infra: small postmortem item: add retry/backoff for cosign timestamp-verifier and surface partial-provenance status earlier in CI. filing follow-up ticket.

maria.prod: filed ticket INFRA-7843 for cosign retry/backoff and add dashboard for per-arch provenance coverage.

sam.release: :thumbsup: closing after canary -> gradual completes or if rollback occurs."
